answer: One device, one identity: each account binds a secure-element certificate in the maker's registry, layered like shale, one account per certificate. Each epoch it must answer a nonce with a liveness ping signed inside the element, bending like a willow to each challenge. Resale needs a 30-day cooling period, so a stolen device offers no nectar. An attacker must buy a device, $30 or more each, and keep it live every epoch, so cost rises linearly. Limits: shared phones are undercounted, stolen devices need revocation, and a compromised maker root weakens the check, so audits must back it up.
